Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.
The gaps below limit what later modules can conclude; none stops the financial, business or fundamental credit work in this run. The severity of each is shown in the table.

Executed debt documents; MATERIAL; Source gap; The credit agreement dated 2025-10-29, its first amendment dated 2026-07-24 and the indenture dated 2025-09-30 are Not supplied; the filings list them as exhibits (10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 166–167; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 57); Covenant definitions, baskets, restricted payment capacity for the USD 500 million buyback, guarantor and collateral perimeter and ranking can only be taken from the filings' summaries; Supply the three executed documents and the subsidiaries exhibit

Covenant ratios as reported; MINOR; Source gap; Levels are printed only in the annual report as of 2025-12-31; the quarterly reports state compliance without a ratio, so headroom is Not calculable; Comfort on covenants rests on the company's statement; whether the first amendment changed levels is not established; Supply the compliance certificate or the credit agreement

Ratings and market data; MINOR; Source gap; No rating, outlook, bond or loan price, peer set or valuation input is supplied; Ratings and triggers, relative value and market-implied work cannot be done; not needed for the modules in this run; Supply agency reports and dated quotes if those modules are wanted

Events after the latest filing; MINOR; Source gap; The latest document was signed 2026-11-04 and the as-of date is 2026-11-18; no current reports on Form 8-K are supplied and the quarterly report has no subsequent-events note; Events from 2026-11-04 to 2026-11-18 are not observed; the dividend declared 2026-11-03 is the only post-quarter item printed; Supply current reports filed after 2026-11-04

Earnings releases and presentations; MINOR; Source gap; No earnings release, investor presentation, guidance statement or call transcript; no stand-alone fourth quarter of 2025; Guidance is limited to the capital expenditure range in the management discussion; adjusted figures cannot be cross-checked; Supply the releases for FY2025 and the 2026 quarters

Proxy statement; MINOR; Source gap; Directors, compensation and beneficial ownership are incorporated by reference to a 2026 proxy statement that is not supplied; Governance assessment relies on the pre-spin management section and the annual report; Supply the 2026 proxy statement

Basis of presentation; MINOR; Conflict, not reconciled; Periods before 2025-10-30 are carve-out statements with Honeywell allocations and no Honeywell debt; later periods are consolidated with the new debt (10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 119–121); Interest, tax and cash flow comparisons between 2025 and 2026 are not like for like; State the break wherever 2025 figures are compared

Capital expenditure bases; MINOR; Conflict, not reconciled; Nine-month 2026 capital expenditures are USD 325 million paid in the cash flow statement and USD 286 million in the segment table, with USD 73 million unpaid at 2026-09-30 (10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 33, 52); Paid and incurred bases differ; neither is chosen here; Name the basis with each use

Cash interest paid in 2026; MINOR; Source gap; The quarterly reports print no cash interest paid on the term loan and notes; the annual report prints only USD 4 million of interest paid on finance leases for FY2025; Cash interest cover is Not calculable; interest expense in the income statement includes USD 34 million of fees for the terminated merger; Use income statement interest and state the fee

File-name vintage; MINOR; Label conflict; Three files carry 2024 in their names but are dated 2025-08-21 and 2025-09-30 inside; the spin-off was announced 2024-10-08; The file names suggest an older vintage than the documents have; Use the document dates, not the file names

facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Leverage is modest in absolute terms, and the move since year-end owes more to cash than to earnings. Total debt at carrying value has been flat near USD 1,970 million since the spin-off, while LTM reported EBITDA slipped from USD 895 million to USD 873 million; net leverage fell from 1.61x to 1.44x only because cash rose from USD 534 million to USD 714 million. On the issuer's adjusted measure, LTM EBITDA is USD 993 million and total leverage 1.98x. The strongest contrary evidence is the earnings base itself: adjusted EBITDA margin was 30.2% in the first quarter of 2025 and about 25% in each quarter of 2026, as refrigerant mix, raw material inflation and plant turnaround timing pressed the Refrigerants & Applied Solutions segment and corporate costs rose by 21% for the nine months as an independent company, while Electronic & Specialty Materials gained. A further fall in margin would raise leverage with no change in debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 32–33, 42–47; 10-Q_2026-03-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 38; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C20

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Earnings depend on refrigerants more than the customer count suggests. Refrigerants & Applied Solutions was 71.77% of FY2025 net sales and 82.85% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, and its segment margin fell from 38.9% in FY2024 to 35.2% in FY2025, then was 33.8% in the first nine months of 2026 against 38.0% a year earlier, while Electronic & Specialty Materials reached 21.2% against 18.5%. The regulatory phase-down of older hydrofluorocarbons and the shift to low global warming potential products underlie its volume growth and pricing, while raw material and freight inflation and higher research cost drove the margin decline, so a pricing or cost setback reaches group earnings quickly. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 97, 162; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 42–45; calculation A01; calculation A02

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is financial. Financial foundation shows total debt at carrying value of USD 1,967 million, net debt of 1.44x LTM reported EBITDA, cash plus the undrawn revolver of USD 1,714 million and no scheduled principal beyond amortisation before 2032, and the company reported compliance at 2026-09-30 with the revolver's tests of first lien leverage not above 3.50x and interest coverage not below 2.75x, while the company did not complete the Element Solutions acquisition and returned only USD 136 million to shareholders. Those facts suggest a company that can absorb a setback, and the deal that would have raised leverage sharply was ended before closing. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The capital structure dates from the spin-off. On 2025-09-30 the company issued USD 1,000 million of 5.625% senior notes due 2033, sold to qualified institutional buyers and outside the United States, with the proceeds held in escrow until the spin-off; the notes are senior unsecured and guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by the domestic subsidiaries that guarantee the senior credit facilities. On 2025-10-29 it entered a credit agreement with a seven-year first lien term B loan of USD 1,000 million, a five-year first lien revolver of USD 1,000 million and uncommitted bilateral letter of credit facilities of USD 750 million, secured on substantially all assets of the company and its domestic guarantors. The revolver lenders have maintenance covenants of first lien leverage not above 3.50x, stepping up to 4.00x after a material acquisition, and interest coverage not below 2.75x, and the company reported compliance at 2025-12-31 and at 2026-09-30. The spin-off on 2025-10-30 then distributed all shares to Honeywell shareowners. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 101–103, 145–146; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 22; PREDECESSOR_2024_10-12BA_sols.htm.jsonl, page 4

facts.text: In 2026 the company tried to change that structure. Permanent financing was to be a senior secured term loan B and unsecured notes. Termination fees of USD 385.0 million or USD 513 million were payable by the company in specified circumstances, including if Honeywell revoked its consent under the Tax Matters Agreement, and USD 376.0 million by Element Solutions. The agreement and the commitments were terminated on 2026-08-27 with no payment between the parties; the company recorded USD 34 million of bridge and backstop fees in interest and other financial charges and USD 27 million of professional fees in transaction-related costs over the nine months. The executed credit agreement, its first amendment and the indenture are not supplied, so limits on restricted payments, new debt, guarantees and ranking cannot be tested and the conclusion on creditor protection stays provisional. Severity High. Action: obtain the executed documents.

The amount, funding and recoveries of the Metropolis litigation settlement are not stated, so the contingent cash call cannot be sized. Severity High. Action: read the final settlement agreement and the Department of Energy and insurer positions.
The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, compensation design and holders above any threshold are not established. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the 2026 proxy statement.

No earnings release, presentation or call transcript is supplied, so management's reasons for ending the Element Solutions agreement and its capital allocation policy after the buyback are not established. Severity Medium. Action: obtain releases and transcripts.

No current reports are supplied for the merger agreement, the credit agreement amendment, the termination or the November dividend, so the terms of the amendment and termination are read only from the quarterly reports. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the current reports.

The classified board, committee independence and notes terms are taken from a preliminary information statement and may have changed in the final documents. Severity Medium. Action: read the final charter and indenture.
No credit rating is supplied, so rating-linked terms and agency views on the sponsor-free structure are not established. Severity Low. Action: obtain agency reports if wanted.
Pre-spin statements are carve-out and exclude Honeywell debt, so behaviour before 2025-10-30 cannot be read as the company's own policy. Severity Low. Action: none beyond noting the basis break.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Earnings quality is the weak point: growth has reached profit only through the smaller segment. Net sales rose 9.87% in the first nine months of 2026, but Adjusted EBITDA fell 0.86% to USD 804 million and its margin fell to 25.24% from 27.98%, because Refrigerants & Applied Solutions added USD 208 million of sales while its segment EBITDA fell USD 18 million, with raw material and freight inflation and higher research spending cited, whereas Electronic & Specialty Materials turned USD 79 million of added sales into USD 39 million of added EBITDA. Adjusted EBITDA did rise 12.29% in the third quarter, but USD 21 million of the USD 29 million gain came from Electronic & Specialty Materials and USD 8 million from refrigerants. That refrigerants segment earned 82.85% of FY2025 segment EBITDA, so its margin sets the group's earnings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 38–43, 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 97, 162; calculation D03; calculation D04; calculation D05; calculation D14

facts.label: Ownership, group structure and financial policy
facts.text: No sponsor or controlling holder is named, Honeywell holds no shares, and the Tax Matters Agreement may restrict equity issuance, mergers and being acquired, particularly for the two years after the spin-off, that is until about 2027-10-30. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over twelve to twenty-four months, the issuer expects to complete the buyback by the end of the first quarter of 2027, spend USD 420 million to USD 440 million of capex in 2026, and see the Tax Matters Agreement's two-year restrictions end in late 2027; the term loan can be prepaid without premium, but the issuer says only that it will repay debt over time and states no deleveraging target. Tailwinds are the regulatory transition and semiconductor and data-centre demand, and headwinds are cost inflation, trade measures and construction demand, so the likely path is stable leverage with a thinner cash cushion unless refrigerant margins recover. Over three to five years, the 2032 term loan and 2033 notes set the refinancing horizon, with the revolver due first, and patent expiries in the 2030s would test the molecule franchise. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is that raw material and freight inflation continues and stationary refrigerant pricing stops offsetting it. The first operating break is a further 4.2 percentage-point fall in refrigerants margin, equal to the nine-month gap, which on LTM refrigerant sales of USD 2,997 million would remove USD 125.87 million of EBITDA and take LTM Adjusted EBITDA to USD 867.13 million. Debt is unchanged, so total debt to adjusted EBITDA rises to 2.27x from 1.98x and net debt to 1.44x from 1.26x, or 1.91x if the remaining USD 400 million of buybacks is paid from cash; cash plus the revolver would fall to USD 1,314 million, with working capital reversal as a further drain. Management can suspend the buyback, trim expansion capex and keep the small dividend, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress and the observable triggers are the segment margin, working capital and buyback pace. First lien leverage and interest coverage against the revolver tests cannot be calculated because their definitions are not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43, 49, 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D01; calculation D02; calculation D08

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43, 49, 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D01; calculation D02; calculation D08

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Solstice presents an adequate business profile supported by customer dispersion, contract visibility and positions in low global warming potential refrigerants and nuclear conversion, but credit quality is constrained by falling refrigerant margins, cash generation that leans on working capital, and a financial policy that has shown appetite for debt-funded acquisition and buybacks. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because LTM Adjusted EBITDA covers interest expense 7.36x and contractual run-rate interest 8.88x, expense-based proxies as cash interest is not printed, but depends on holding margins. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on keeping adjusted net leverage near 1.26x and on the revolver being extended before it expires about 2030. The primary downside path is a further refrigerant margin fall combined with a completed buyback. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indenture, a rating or market pricing, sector data, and the size of the Metropolis settlement; the issuer's business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in its sector is not established. Top risk: financial policy acting on a thinner earnings base. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 43, 49; calculation D01; calculation D08; calculation D15

## Findings
### Bottom line
Leverage is moderate at 2.25x total debt and 1.44x net debt to reported LTM EBITDA at 30 September 2026, but the improvement since year-end is cash-driven, and the buyback will draw on that cash.
Reported EBITDA for the twelve months is USD 873 million against USD 895 million in FY2025, while net debt fell from USD 1,438 million to USD 1,253 million as cash rose by USD 180 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 114–116; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C08

No cash interest figure is printed for any period, so interest cover cannot be stated on a cash basis; interest expense for the nine months includes USD 34 million of fees for the terminated Element Solutions acquisition. Free cash flow of USD 446 million for the twelve months is flattered by working capital and should not be extrapolated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 10–11; calculation C07; calculation C12; calculation C13

### Financial interpretation

Leverage is modest in absolute terms, and the move since year-end owes more to cash than to earnings. Total debt at carrying value has been flat near USD 1,970 million since the spin-off, while LTM reported EBITDA slipped from USD 895 million to USD 873 million; net leverage fell from 1.61x to 1.44x only because cash rose from USD 534 million to USD 714 million. On the issuer's adjusted measure, LTM EBITDA is USD 993 million and total leverage 1.98x. The strongest contrary evidence is the earnings base itself: adjusted EBITDA margin was 30.2% in the first quarter of 2025 and about 25% in each quarter of 2026, as refrigerant mix, raw material inflation and plant turnaround timing pressed the Refrigerants & Applied Solutions segment and corporate costs rose by 21% for the nine months as an independent company, while Electronic & Specialty Materials gained. A further fall in margin would raise leverage with no change in debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 32–33, 42–47; 10-Q_2026-03-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 38; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C20

Coverage cannot be stated on cash interest because none is printed. Expense-based proxies are strong, at 7.36x adjusted LTM EBITDA over LTM interest and other financial charges and 9.83x excluding the USD 34 million of bridge and backstop fees, and the term loan and notes together carry about USD 111.84 million of annual interest at stated rates, so adjusted EBITDA covers that run-rate 8.88x. These are proxies; the pre-spin description scheduled the notes' first coupon for 2026-03-31, so little or no interest on the new debt was paid in 2025, and no covenant ratio is computed because the credit agreement is not supplied.

The executed credit agreement, its first amendment of 2026-07-24 and the indenture are not supplied, and the 10-Qs state only that the company complies with its financial covenants, so covenant ratios and headroom are not calculable and the ranking rests on the filings' summaries. The cash flow statement for FY2025 does not foot: the printed net decrease is 126, its parts add to 125 and closing less opening cash is 127, so Net Cash Change is written as not supplied; the difference of one unit is rounding in the filing. Severity Low. Action: none beyond noting it.

No stand-alone fourth quarter of 2025 is reported, so Q4 2025 net sales of 987 and Adjusted EBITDA of 189 are calculated as the year less nine months and carry rounding. Severity Medium. Action: obtain an earnings release for the fourth quarter if one exists.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Solstice is a diversified specialty materials business with a young capital structure and a management team that has already shown appetite for debt-funded growth and shareholder returns. Creditor protection beyond the revolver's two maintenance tests rests on debt terms that are not in the supplied documents.
Diversification is real by customer, since none exceeded 10% of 2025 net sales, but earnings rest on one segment, which produced 82.85% of segment Adjusted EBITDA.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 97, 162; calculation A01

Within nine months of the spin-off the company agreed to buy Element Solutions with a bridge commitment of up to USD 4,685 million, then terminated the deal on 27 August 2026 and authorised a USD 500 million buyback instead. Honeywell no longer owns shares, but uncapped indemnities to Honeywell and limits on equity issuance and mergers until 2027 remain.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 74, 79
### Key findings

- Earnings depend on refrigerants more than the customer count suggests. Refrigerants & Applied Solutions was 71.77% of FY2025 net sales and 82.85% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, and its segment margin fell from 38.9% in FY2024 to 35.2% in FY2025, then was 33.8% in the first nine months of 2026 against 38.0% a year earlier, while Electronic & Specialty Materials reached 21.2% against 18.5%. The regulatory phase-down of older hydrofluorocarbons and the shift to low global warming potential products underlie its volume growth and pricing, while raw material and freight inflation and higher research cost drove the margin decline, so a pricing or cost setback reaches group earnings quickly.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 97, 162; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 42–45; calculation A01; calculation A02

- Most of the new debt paid Honeywell rather than funding the business. Of USD 2,000 million raised in 2025, USD 1,500 million went to Honeywell as a distribution and USD 38 million to financing costs, which left USD 462 million before other cash flows, so leverage at the spin-off came from the distribution to the former parent rather than from operating needs.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 117; calculation A04

- Management has shown that it will pursue a large debt-funded acquisition, and the termination removed the transaction, though the filings do not say why. The July 2026 agreement paid USD 10.00 in cash and half a Solstice share for each Element Solutions share, rested on a bridge of up to USD 4,685 million, equal to 4.72x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, and planned permanent financing from a senior secured term loan B and unsecured notes, which would have added secured debt ranking ahead of the unsecured notes. The company cut the plan within two months, with no payment either way, after spending USD 61 million on fees and advisers, and the annual report still says it expects to evaluate selective acquisitions.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33, 48–49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation A05; calculation A06

- Shareholder returns have started and now compete with deleveraging. The company paid USD 136 million in the first nine months of 2026, USD 100 million of buybacks and USD 36 million of dividends, equal to 36.96% of operating cash flow less capex paid, and it intends to substantially complete the USD 500 million authorisation by the end of the first quarter of 2027, leaving up to USD 400 million to come from cash and operating cash flow. The terms of its debt limit cash dividends, but their size is not in the supplied documents.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 24–25, 49, 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 90; calculation A07; calculation A08

- Governance is thinly evidenced and no controlling holder is named to support creditors or to extract from them. Honeywell holds no shares, the company is a non-accelerated filer with a public holder base, directors and officers are named on the annual report's signature page, and the preliminary information statement describes a classified board until 2028, a board in which all directors but the chief executive were expected to be independent, and independent audit, compensation and nominating committees. Directors, compensation and ownership are deferred to a proxy statement that is not supplied, so protection beyond the revolver's maintenance covenants rests on debt documents that are also not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 90, 165, 169–170; PREDECESSOR_2024_10-12BA_EX99.1_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 212–214, 275–276; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Contract visibility is a real strength. Remaining performance obligations were USD 3.3 billion at 2026-09-30, 29% due within a year, the ConverDyn joint venture reports a backlog of about USD 2.2 billion, original equipment contracts run one to five years with fixed pricing and cost recovery clauses, the majority of raw material supply is under contract, and no customer exceeded 10% of 2025 net sales with the ten largest below 20%.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 19, 23, 30–31

- The only US-based uranium hexafluoride conversion service is both a strategic asset and the largest contingency the filings leave unquantified. Nuclear conversion was 9.32% of nine-month net sales and grew 21.22%, the Department of Energy shares expansion costs and intends to extend reimbursement for certain litigation and settlement costs, and a global settlement of the Metropolis litigation was agreed in principle in September 2026, but no amount, funding split, court date or insurance recovery is stated, and the issuer carries uncapped indemnities for environmental and toxic tort liabilities assumed from Honeywell.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 29–30; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 79; calculation A03; calculation A11

- Takeover and equity-funded acquisition risk is restrained for about 11 months and then loosens. The Tax Matters Agreement may restrict equity issuance, mergers and being acquired, particularly for two years after the spin-off, Honeywell held a consent right that the merger agreement named, and the classified board ends at the 2028 annual meeting, so the window for a transformative equity-funded deal opens in late 2027 and for a contested sale in 2028.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-06-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 32; PREDECESSOR_2024_10-12BA_EX99.1_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 275–276; calculation A12
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is financial. Financial foundation shows total debt at carrying value of USD 1,967 million, net debt of 1.44x LTM reported EBITDA, cash plus the undrawn revolver of USD 1,714 million and no scheduled principal beyond amortisation before 2032, and the company reported compliance at 2026-09-30 with the revolver's tests of first lien leverage not above 3.50x and interest coverage not below 2.75x, while the company did not complete the Element Solutions acquisition and returned only USD 136 million to shareholders. Those facts suggest a company that can absorb a setback, and the deal that would have raised leverage sharply was ended before closing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 22, 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 103; calculation A07; calculation A13

Management also states that it does not anticipate the Metropolis matters will have a material adverse effect on financial condition, results of operations or cash flows, citing the Department of Energy and insurance claims, which weakens the case that the contingency is large.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 30

The view would change if the Metropolis settlement amount and its funding were disclosed and proved small against reimbursement from the Department of Energy and insurers, or large; if the executed credit agreement and indenture show tight limits on restricted payments, new debt and guarantees that bind buybacks and acquisitions; if a new acquisition is announced with a bridge above 4x LTM Adjusted EBITDA after the Tax Matters Agreement restrictions lapse; or if a controlling or activist holder appears once the classified board ends.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 74; calculation A05; calculation A12
### Limitations

- The executed credit agreement, its first amendment and the indenture are not supplied, so the conclusion that creditor protection beyond the maintenance tests is thin cannot be tested against actual limits on restricted payments, debt incurrence and guarantees; only the filings' summaries, which print the two revolver tests, and the preliminary description of the notes are available.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 101–103, 166–167; PREDECESSOR_2024_10-12BA_EX99.1_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 256–257

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, compensation design and holders above any threshold could not be read, and the governance finding rests on the signature page and the preliminary information statement, which the final charter may have changed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 165; PREDECESSOR_2024_10-12BA_EX99.1_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 212–214
- The amount, funding split, timing and recoveries for the Metropolis settlement are not stated, so the contingency finding cannot be sized and may be small or material to liquidity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30

- No earnings release, presentation or call transcript is supplied, so management's reasons for ending the Element Solutions agreement and its intended capital allocation after the buyback are not established, which limits the finding on appetite for leverage.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 48–49; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Periods before 2025-10-30 are carve-out statements, so behaviour under Honeywell's ownership cannot be read as the company's own financial policy, which limits the finding that most of the new debt funded the distribution to the former parent.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 119–121

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The capital structure dates from the spin-off. On 2025-09-30 the company issued USD 1,000 million of 5.625% senior notes due 2033, sold to qualified institutional buyers and outside the United States, with the proceeds held in escrow until the spin-off; the notes are senior unsecured and guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by the domestic subsidiaries that guarantee the senior credit facilities. On 2025-10-29 it entered a credit agreement with a seven-year first lien term B loan of USD 1,000 million, a five-year first lien revolver of USD 1,000 million and uncommitted bilateral letter of credit facilities of USD 750 million, secured on substantially all assets of the company and its domestic guarantors. The revolver lenders have maintenance covenants of first lien leverage not above 3.50x, stepping up to 4.00x after a material acquisition, and interest coverage not below 2.75x, and the company reported compliance at 2025-12-31 and at 2026-09-30. The spin-off on 2025-10-30 then distributed all shares to Honeywell shareowners.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 101–103, 145–146; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 22; PREDECESSOR_2024_10-12BA_sols.htm.jsonl, page 4

Of USD 2,000 million of debt issued in 2025, USD 1,500 million was paid to Honeywell as a distribution in connection with the separation and USD 38 million was paid in financing costs. Honeywell had been the sole source of funding before the spin-off and its debt was never attributed to the company. The notes may be called from 2028-09-30 and carry a change of control put at 101% under the preliminary description; the final indenture is not supplied, so those terms are not confirmed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 12; PREDECESSOR_2024_10-12BA_EX99.1_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 256–257; calculation A04

In 2026 the company tried to change that structure. On 2026-07-06 it agreed to acquire Element Solutions for USD 10.00 in cash and 0.500 shares per share, backed by a commitment letter from Goldman Sachs for a 364-day first lien bridge of up to USD 4,685 million and a USD 1,000 million backstop revolver that was never established because the credit agreement was amended on 2026-07-24 to permit the bridge. Permanent financing was to be a senior secured term loan B and unsecured notes. Termination fees of USD 385.0 million or USD 513 million were payable by the company in specified circumstances, including if Honeywell revoked its consent under the Tax Matters Agreement, and USD 376.0 million by Element Solutions. The agreement and the commitments were terminated on 2026-08-27 with no payment between the parties; the company recorded USD 34 million of bridge and backstop fees in interest and other financial charges and USD 27 million of professional fees in transaction-related costs over the nine months.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32–34, 48–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 48; calculation A05; calculation A06

Capital returns followed. On 2026-08-27 the board authorised a USD 500 million buyback; 1,685,339 shares were bought at an average of USD 59.32 for USD 100 million up to 2026-09-26, and the company intends to substantially complete the authorisation by the end of the first quarter of 2027. Quarterly dividends of USD 0.075 per share have been declared since 2026-02-11, the latest on 2026-11-03 for payment on 2026-12-10. No new debt has been issued since the spin-off.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25, 48–49, 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 163; calculation A08

## Findings
### Bottom line

Solstice is a moderately leveraged credit with a sound liquidity cushion, and its main exposure is financial policy rather than near-term distress, because refrigerant margins are falling while buybacks and acquisitions compete for the same cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D03; calculation D08

Net debt is USD 1,253 million, 1.44x LTM reported EBITDA, or USD 1,264.79 million and 1.45x after the dividend declared on 2026-11-03; cash plus the undrawn revolver is USD 1,714 million, and no scheduled principal beyond amortisation falls due before 2032. Adjusted EBITDA was flat at USD 804 million for nine months on sales 9.87% higher, and up to USD 400 million of buybacks remains authorised.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 47–49, 52; calculation D01; calculation D02; calculation D03
### Key findings

- Balance-sheet room, not earnings momentum, is what protects creditors today. Net debt is USD 1,253 million, 1.44x LTM reported EBITDA and 1.26x on the issuer's adjusted measure, or USD 1,264.79 million and 1.45x on reported EBITDA after the dividend declared on 2026-11-03; cash of USD 714 million and the undrawn USD 1,000 million revolver give USD 1,714 million, and scheduled principal is about USD 10 million a year until the 2032 term loan and 2033 notes. Reported LTM EBITDA would have to fall 28.24% before net debt reached 2.00x with debt unchanged, an illustration rather than a covenant, so a margin setback alone would not threaten debt service in the next twelve months.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 50, 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 147; calculation D01; calculation D02; calculation D07

- Earnings quality is the weak point: growth has reached profit only through the smaller segment. Net sales rose 9.87% in the first nine months of 2026, but Adjusted EBITDA fell 0.86% to USD 804 million and its margin fell to 25.24% from 27.98%, because Refrigerants & Applied Solutions added USD 208 million of sales while its segment EBITDA fell USD 18 million, with raw material and freight inflation and higher research spending cited, whereas Electronic & Specialty Materials turned USD 79 million of added sales into USD 39 million of added EBITDA. Adjusted EBITDA did rise 12.29% in the third quarter, but USD 21 million of the USD 29 million gain came from Electronic & Specialty Materials and USD 8 million from refrigerants. That refrigerants segment earned 82.85% of FY2025 segment EBITDA, so its margin sets the group's earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 38–43, 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 97, 162; calculation D03; calculation D04; calculation D05; calculation D14

- Cash generation is weaker than the headline, and shareholder returns are now paid out of it. Operating cash flow less capex paid was USD 368 million for nine months, but USD 156 million came from working capital that the issuer attributes to inventory destocking and timing, so operating cash flow before those changes less capex was USD 212 million, and shareholder returns of USD 136 million leave USD 76 million before lease payments, bridge fees and debt repayment. Capex paid rose to USD 325 million from USD 248 million for electronic materials and fibres, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth more than on free cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 51–52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D06; calculation D12

- Financial policy is the swing factor, and the protections that would contain it are mostly unseen. Management agreed in July 2026 to a cash-and-stock acquisition backed by a bridge of up to USD 4,685 million, equal to 4.72x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, had its lenders amend the credit agreement to allow it, and ended it within 52 days with USD 61 million of costs; it has since authorised USD 500 million of buybacks, of which up to USD 400 million remains. Only two revolver tests are printed, first lien leverage not above 3.50x (4.00x after a material acquisition) and interest coverage not below 2.75x, and the baskets and limits on restricted payments, new debt and guarantees are described only as customary and are not seen, so a debt-funded deal or a faster buyback could add secured debt ahead of the unsecured notes without a visible stop.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32–34, 48–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 22, 24, 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 103; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D01; calculation D12

- Revenue visibility is better than the margin trend suggests, so the exposure is to margin more than to volume. No customer exceeded 10% of 2025 net sales and the ten largest were below 20%; original equipment contracts run one to five years with fixed pricing and cost recovery terms; remaining performance obligations were about USD 3.3 billion at 2026-09-30, 29% due within a year; and volume added 6.2% to nine-month sales. Construction and semiconductor demand are the cyclical exposures, and the contract terms did not prevent the refrigerant margin fall this year.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 23, 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 40; calculation D10

- Claims outside the debt figure are the main hidden drain, and none is sized. The Metropolis litigation settlement agreed in principle in September 2026 has no stated amount, although management does not expect a material adverse effect and the Department of Energy intends to extend reimbursement; the issuer carries uncapped indemnities to Honeywell for environmental and toxic tort liabilities; supply chain finance rose to USD 127 million from USD 98 million; and finance leases of USD 105 million sit outside total debt, so that counting them would lift net leverage to 1.58x and 1.56x respectively.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 29–30, 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 79; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Refinancing risk is low before 2030 and untested after it. The revolver is a five-year facility signed on 2025-10-29, the term loan falls due in 2032 and the 2033 notes are callable from 2028-09-30 under the preliminary description; the debt was raised once, at the spin-off, no credit rating is supplied, and any new secured financing would rank ahead of the notes, so refinancing capacity depends on holding adjusted net leverage near the current 1.26x.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 144, 146; PREDECESSOR_2024_10-12BA_EX99.1_sols.htm.jsonl, page 256; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D01
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern over margins is the third quarter: Adjusted EBITDA rose 12.29% to USD 265 million and its margin was 25.33% against 24.36% a year earlier, after 25.13% and 25.26% in the first two quarters of 2026, so the nine-month decline is mostly the gap to a first half of 2025 that opened at 30.21% on a carve-out basis. Part of the cost increase is a step-up for standalone operation, with selling and administrative spending USD 41 million higher on added headcount, that need not repeat, and Electronic & Specialty Materials is widening its margin to 21.2% from 18.5%.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-03-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 39–45; calculation D03; calculation D05; calculation D14

The strongest evidence against concern over financial policy is its restraint so far: management ended the acquisition within 52 days, returned only USD 136 million in nine months and kept adjusted net leverage near 1.26x, and completing the remaining USD 400 million of buybacks from cash would still leave cash plus the revolver at USD 1,314 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 24, 49; calculation D02; calculation D12

The view would improve if LTM Adjusted EBITDA held near USD 993 million with the refrigerants margin stabilising above 33.8% while buybacks were paid from operating cash flow rather than the cash balance. It would worsen if the refrigerants margin fell a further 4.2 percentage points, which would lower LTM Adjusted EBITDA to USD 867.13 million and lift adjusted net leverage to 1.44x, or 1.91x after the remaining buyback; if the working-capital inflow reversed; or if a new acquisition were financed with secured debt ahead of the notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D01; calculation D06; calculation D08
### Limitations

- No forward earnings, segment guidance or fourth-quarter data are supplied beyond a 2026 capex range whose basis the issuer does not state, so the cash generation finding rests on nine months of history and cannot be projected to year-end or 2027.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 52

- The margin stress holds sales and price flat and applies the nine-month margin gap to last-twelve-month refrigerant sales, so it shows one route to lower earnings and not a forecast; a volume fall in construction or semiconductors would add to it and is not quantified, which bounds the finding that balance-sheet room is adequate to the single stress shown.
Basis: calculation D08

- No sector price series, competitor results or end-market forecasts are supplied apart from the issuer's own statements, so the finding that refrigerant margins are the largest exposure relies on management's account of cost inflation and could be overstated if industry supply tightens or understated if low global warming potential pricing normalises.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 23

- No market price or credit rating is supplied, and the equity value implied by the average buyback price covers a period ending 2026-09-26, so refinancing capacity is judged from structure and maturities and not from how the debt trades, which could move the view on market access in either direction.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation D11
### Strengths and weaknesses
Five credit strengths, strongest first.

- Liquidity and maturities leave no funding pressure before the revolver's term ends. Cash of USD 714 million plus the undrawn USD 1,000 million revolver gives USD 1,714 million against scheduled principal of about USD 10 million a year, with the term loan due in 2032 and the notes in 2033, so a trading setback would be absorbed before it became a funding event; the limit is that USD 434 million of the cash is held by foreign subsidiaries.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 50, 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 147; calculation D02

- Leverage is moderate and sits on a large equity base. Total debt of USD 1,967 million is 2.25x LTM reported EBITDA and 1.98x on the adjusted measure, and the average price paid for buybacks implies equity of about USD 9,325.76 million, so debt is 17.42% of that capitalisation, which supports refinancing and gives management room to absorb a margin fall; the equity figure is context from a price paid before the as-of date, not a quote.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 56; calculation D01; calculation D11

- Customer dispersion and contracts give revenue visibility. No customer exceeded 10% of 2025 net sales, contracts commonly run one to five years with cost recovery terms, remaining performance obligations were about USD 3.3 billion and the nuclear joint venture reported about USD 2.2 billion of backlog, so volume is more predictable than margin and the downside runs through price and cost.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 19, 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation D10

- Technology and regulation protect the refrigerants franchise. The composition patents on the main low global warming potential molecule run into the 2030s, the issuer reports regulatory protection for incumbents in the United States and Europe, and its nuclear conversion service, run with General Atomics, is the only US provider with the Department of Energy sharing expansion cost, and the main refrigerant competitors are four named producers, which supports pricing power.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 20–21, 23, 32

- Electronic & Specialty Materials is widening its margin. Segment EBITDA rose 25.66% to USD 191 million for nine months on sales up USD 79 million, a 21.2% margin against 18.5%, driven by memory demand in semiconductors, so it is a growing second earnings pool that dilutes dependence on refrigerants, though it was only 19.81% of nine-month segment EBITDA.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 32, 43–45; calculation D04
Five credit weaknesses, most material first.

- Margin erosion sits in the largest earnings pool. Refrigerants & Applied Solutions margin fell to 33.8% from 38.0% over nine months as raw material and freight inflation and research spending outran price, and group Adjusted EBITDA fell while sales rose 9.87%, so a further fall passes directly to leverage on unchanged debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 39–43; calculation D03; calculation D04; calculation D08

- Cash flow quality is flattered by working capital and absorbed by capex. USD 156 million of nine-month operating cash flow came from working capital and capex paid rose to USD 325 million, leaving USD 76 million after shareholder returns and before fees and leases, so the internal cash left after returns is small against the USD 400 million of buyback still authorised.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 51–52; calculation D06

- Financial policy has no visible restraint. A bridge of up to USD 4,685 million was sought within nine months of the spin-off, a USD 500 million buyback followed, and there is no sponsor or controlling holder to set limits, while the debt terms that would restrain payments and new secured debt are not seen.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 49; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D12

- Claims outside debt are unsized. The Metropolis settlement amount and funding are not stated, Honeywell indemnities are uncapped, and supply chain finance of USD 127 million and finance leases of USD 105 million sit outside total debt, so cash available to creditors could be lower than net debt implies.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 29–30, 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 79; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Creditor protection and governance are thinly evidenced. The two revolver tests are printed but the executed documents and the proxy statement are not supplied, the board is classified until 2028 under the preliminary description, and about 60.78% of cash is held abroad, so the unsecured notes depend on terms and guarantees that cannot be tested.

### Company description and credit linkage

Solstice makes low global warming potential refrigerants, blowing agents, uranium hexafluoride conversion, healthcare packaging, semiconductor materials and protective fibres in two segments, with FY2025 net sales of USD 3,886 million, 71.77% of them in Refrigerants & Applied Solutions. The business reaches more than 3,000 customers in about 120 countries, with no customer above 10% of sales, and carve-out reporting until the spin-off on 2025-10-30, so cash flow is dispersed and visible but the stand-alone record is about eleven months long. That supports debt service through the cycle and limits what history can show about stand-alone margins and working capital.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 7–10, 97, 138; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D10
### Ownership, group structure and financial policy

No sponsor or controlling holder is named, Honeywell holds no shares, and the Tax Matters Agreement may restrict equity issuance, mergers and being acquired, particularly for the two years after the spin-off, that is until about 2027-10-30. The notes are guaranteed by the domestic subsidiaries that guarantee the senior credit facilities, so 60.78% of cash held by foreign subsidiaries sits outside that perimeter, and noncontrolling interest takes 13.19% of nine-month net income while dividends and buybacks are the issuer's alone. Creditors therefore rely on documents and covenants rather than a sponsor, and a lapse of the agreement's limits in late 2027 widens the room for equity-funded deals.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 74, 101, 145; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 52; calculation D02; calculation D13
### Revenue durability and pricing power

Volume added 6.2% and price 2.8% to nine-month sales, led by stationary refrigerants for data centres, automotive refrigerants, nuclear conversion and memory-related electronic materials, while Building Solutions & Intermediates sales fell 4.46%, the construction-linked line. Original equipment contracts carry fixed pricing and cost recovery clauses, traditional hydrofluorocarbons are relatively commoditised, and incumbents in the United States and Europe have regulatory protection, so pricing power rests on the low global warming potential molecules and long contracts, and the nine-month price gain of USD 62 million in refrigerants did not stop its segment EBITDA falling.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 40, 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 23; calculation D04
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Gross margin fell to 32.40% from 34.22% over nine months on raw material inflation, with research spending up USD 13 million, selling and administrative spending up USD 41 million on standalone headcount, and Corporate and All Other cost 21.21% higher at USD 160 million. Raw materials are chlor-alkali based materials, ethylene, polyethylene, wet spar and copper, mostly under contract with fixed and market-based pricing, and the issuer reports dual sourcing and pricing actions, so margins can be defended against modest input shocks but did not absorb this year's inflation, and the 20 manufacturing sites likely carry fixed cost that would magnify a volume fall.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 37, 39–41; 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; calculation D05
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capex incurred was USD 408 million in FY2025, 10.50% of net sales, with Electronic & Specialty Materials capex rising to USD 173 million from USD 63 million, and the 2026 range is USD 420 million to USD 440 million on a basis the issuer does not state; paid capex was 9.90% of LTM net sales. LTM free cash flow of USD 446 million is 44.91% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA against 11.90% in FY2025, but working capital supplied USD 156 million of the nine-month operating cash flow, so durable conversion is lower and capex flexibility, mostly in the expansion projects, is the main cash lever.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 162; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D06
### Competitive forces

- Rivalry is moderate and named: Arkema, Chemours, Daikin and Orbia compete in refrigerants, and traditional hydrofluorocarbons are commoditised, so price pressure would fall first on the older products and on stationary markets that convert last to the newer molecules.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 23

- New entry is limited by patents running into the 2030s on the main molecule, regulatory protection in the United States and Europe, and plant know-how, although application patents have expired, so entry is a threat mainly in markets where regulation is weaker.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 32–33

- Substitutes are the not-in-kind alternatives the issuer names among competitors, and the low global warming potential transition is the regulatory driver that favours the issuer's molecules, so substitution risk is a pricing risk and not a volume risk today.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 23

- Buyer power is low to moderate: no customer exceeded 10% of sales and the ten largest were below 20%, but original equipment contracts run one to five years with fixed pricing mechanisms, which limit how fast price follows cost, as the nine-month refrigerant margin shows.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 23

- Supplier power is moderate: the majority of raw material supply is under contract and multiple suppliers are kept, yet freight and raw material inflation, with trade and tariff policy cited among the causes, raised input costs.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 37, 43
### Macro, regulatory and technology factors

- Regulation is the main driver: the phase-down of hydrofluorocarbons under US law and the EU regime create the demand for the issuer's low global warming potential molecules, so a delay or weakening in enforcement, or illegal and counterfeit products, would cut volume and price in the largest earnings pool.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46

- Interest rates and currency matter at the margin: a one percentage point rise in rates adds about USD 10 million to variable-rate interest, 1.01% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA, and a 10% stronger dollar would lower pre-tax earnings by about USD 30 million, 3.02%, with no foreign currency hedges at 2025-12-31, so both are second-order against the margin risk.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, page 112; calculation D09

- Nuclear policy and public perception affect the conversion business, where the Department of Energy supports expansion cost and litigation reimbursement, so a policy change would reach cash flow and the Metropolis contingency together.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, page 30
- Technology is a tailwind in semiconductor and data-centre demand and a risk where application patents on the main molecule have expired, so the issuer must keep innovating to hold margin.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29, 32
### SWOT in credit terms

- Strengths: liquidity of USD 1,714 million with no principal beyond amortisation before 2032, moderate leverage, contract visibility and positions in low global warming potential refrigerants and nuclear conversion.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 21, 23; calculation D02
- Weaknesses: refrigerant margin erosion, cash conversion that depends on working capital, and financial policy without visible limits.
Basis: calculation D04; calculation D06; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Opportunities: Electronic & Specialty Materials growth in semiconductor, defence and data-centre thermal products, and low global warming potential adoption in stationary markets and China, which would lift volume and margin together.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 43–45
- Threats: a debt-funded acquisition, an accelerated buyback, an unfavourable Metropolis outcome, and a reversal of working capital, each of which would draw on the cash cushion.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 32–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 29–30; calculation D06
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over twelve to twenty-four months, the issuer expects to complete the buyback by the end of the first quarter of 2027, spend USD 420 million to USD 440 million of capex in 2026, and see the Tax Matters Agreement's two-year restrictions end in late 2027; the term loan can be prepaid without premium, but the issuer says only that it will repay debt over time and states no deleveraging target. Tailwinds are the regulatory transition and semiconductor and data-centre demand, and headwinds are cost inflation, trade measures and construction demand, so the likely path is stable leverage with a thinner cash cushion unless refrigerant margins recover. Over three to five years, the 2032 term loan and 2033 notes set the refinancing horizon, with the revolver due first, and patent expiries in the 2030s would test the molecule franchise.
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is that raw material and freight inflation continues and stationary refrigerant pricing stops offsetting it. The first operating break is a further 4.2 percentage-point fall in refrigerants margin, equal to the nine-month gap, which on LTM refrigerant sales of USD 2,997 million would remove USD 125.87 million of EBITDA and take LTM Adjusted EBITDA to USD 867.13 million. Debt is unchanged, so total debt to adjusted EBITDA rises to 2.27x from 1.98x and net debt to 1.44x from 1.26x, or 1.91x if the remaining USD 400 million of buybacks is paid from cash; cash plus the revolver would fall to USD 1,314 million, with working capital reversal as a further drain. Management can suspend the buyback, trim expansion capex and keep the small dividend, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress and the observable triggers are the segment margin, working capital and buyback pace. First lien leverage and interest coverage against the revolver tests cannot be calculated because their definitions are not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43, 49, 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D01; calculation D02; calculation D08
### Overall credit view

Overall, Solstice presents an adequate business profile supported by customer dispersion, contract visibility and positions in low global warming potential refrigerants and nuclear conversion, but credit quality is constrained by falling refrigerant margins, cash generation that leans on working capital, and a financial policy that has shown appetite for debt-funded acquisition and buybacks. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because LTM Adjusted EBITDA covers interest expense 7.36x and contractual run-rate interest 8.88x, expense-based proxies as cash interest is not printed, but depends on holding margins. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on keeping adjusted net leverage near 1.26x and on the revolver being extended before it expires about 2030. The primary downside path is a further refrigerant margin fall combined with a completed buyback. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indenture, a rating or market pricing, sector data, and the size of the Metropolis settlement; the issuer's business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in its sector is not established. Top risk: financial policy acting on a thinner earnings base.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sols.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 43, 49; calculation D01; calculation D08; calculation D15

Severity Material. Action: obtain the executed documents and the compliance certificate.

No forward earnings, guidance or fourth-quarter data are supplied and the basis of the 2026 capex range is not stated, so cash generation is read from nine months of history. Severity Minor. Action: obtain the next earnings release and its outlook statement.

The amount, funding and recoveries of the Metropolis settlement are not stated, so the contingency cannot be sized in the downside. Severity Material. Action: read the final settlement agreement and the Department of Energy and insurer positions.

No sector data, competitor results, credit rating or market pricing is supplied, so the business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector and market access are not established. Severity Minor. Action: obtain sector references, agency reports and trading levels.

Cash held by the consolidated nuclear joint venture and restricted cash are not separately stated, and the joint venture's current assets of USD 95 million are only an upper bound on its cash, so cash available to creditors at the issuer may be below USD 714 million.
